title: Fruit Into Baskets / Longest with At Most K Distinct: variable window + char count.
shortTitle: Fruit Into Baskets / Longest With At Most K Distinct: Variable Window + Char Count
keyPoints: Grow the window right, tracking distinct values in a HashMap of value-to-count
When distinct count exceeds K, shrink from the left until at most K distinct values remain
Remove a key from the map when its count drops to zero to keep the distinct measure accurate
Fruit Into Baskets is the K=2 special case of this general pattern
O(n) amortized time because the left pointer only advances; O(K) space for the map
The inner shrink loop trims only as much as needed to restore the at-most-K invariant

s1_definition.oneliner: Expand the window and track distinct counts in a map; when distinct exceeds K, shrink from the left until it is at most K again.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Longest subarray with at most K distinct** – find the longest contiguous subarray containing at most K different values.
- **Fruit Into Baskets** – the special case where K=2, framed as two baskets each holding one fruit type.
- **HashMap tracking** – a map counts occurrences of each value in the window; the map size equals the distinct count.
- **Zero-count removal** – remove a key when its count drops to zero so the map size stays accurate.
- **Complexity** – O(n) time amortized, O(K) space for the map.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India wants the longest run of consecutive card transactions that touches at most K different merchant categories, as a loyalty-pattern signal. Rajesh grows a window and tallies how many distinct categories it holds. When a new category pushes the count past K, he shrinks from the left, removing categories until only K remain.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The longest subarray with at most K distinct values is a variable-size sliding window problem backed by a count map. You grow the window on the right, incrementing the count of each entering value. Whenever the number of distinct values in the window (the map size) exceeds K, you shrink from the left by decrementing counts and advancing the left pointer.

The one detail that must not be forgotten is removing a key from the map when its count drops to zero. The map's size is the distinct measure, so a stale zero-count key overstates distinctness and causes the window to shrink incorrectly. Removing the key keeps the measure exact.

The Fruit Into Baskets problem is literally this with K=2, framed as two baskets each holding one fruit type. Recognizing that specialization shows the interviewer you understand the general pattern rather than memorizing a specific solution.

In the analytics service at the National Bank of India, Rajesh finds the longest run of consecutive card transactions that stay within at most K distinct merchant categories, as a signal of concentrated spending for a targeted reward program. The zero-count key removal keeps the distinct count accurate, and the amortized linear time handles long transaction histories efficiently.

Remember one sentence: expand right tracking distinct counts in a map, shrink left when distinct exceeds K, and always remove zero-count keys to keep the measure accurate.
